rationale: B wins because it turns the missing proof into the story instead of decorating around it; “A profitable fintech is walking into the market that broke the unprofitable ones” gives a reporter a real economics question. A has useful bones, but “Mercury Has 200,000 Business Customers. It Just Started Pitching Them Personally.” invents the cross-sell it should have interrogated, and “Two Years After SVB” botches the clock. B still needs cleanup on overbroad market claims, but it is better strategic material for a founder who wants coverage, not applause.
gaps_in_A: “Two Years After SVB” is factually sloppy. As of June 9, 2026, SVB’s collapse is a three-year arc, not a two-year one.
“built entirely on being the startup-banking alternative” overclaims the update. The facts say Mercury became well known after SVB, not that its whole brand was built there.
“It Just Started Pitching Them Personally” invents targeting and cross-sell behavior. The update says invite-only waitlist; it does not say Mercury is pitching existing business customers.
“runs opposite to the consumer-to-business neobank trajectory most competitors have tried” imports a market thesis without evidence from the update.
gaps_in_B: “market that broke the unprofitable ones” is a sharp frame, but it needs evidence. The update gives Mercury’s profitability claim, not proof that consumer neobanking broke competitors.
“grew on SVB’s collapse” overstates “became well known.” Growth, deposit flows, and causal lift are not supplied.
“now wants your paycheck” assumes primary-checking or payroll positioning. The facts say checking and savings accounts, not paycheck capture.
“live question in fintech-banking supervision” needs a real current regulatory peg. The set admits no current news signal was supplied, then leans on one anyway.
